items.title: SI-assisted galaxy simulations reach 5.4 trillion particles
participants: Other international collaborators named in official report
items.what_changed: New official report documents AI-surrogate-assisted galaxy simulations up to 5.4 trillion particles and Aurora throughput of 144 billion particles per second; Gordon Bell finalist status is secondary to technical results.
items.significance: AI surrogates reduce the cost of resolving supernova feedback, enabling detailed study of star formation and galactic evolution.
items.affiliation_evidence: Official OLCF report credits Director's Discretionary computing allocations and describes AI surrogate models, but identifies no Genesis award or project connection. Searches for ASURA-FDPS-ML and PHEASANT with Genesis and comparison against the 297-project repository registry found no documented linkage. DOE computing use alone is not evidence of Genesis affiliation.
items.deduplication_note: Absent from 36-item archive and 56-candidate science review file; new performance results differ from earlier 300-billion-particle work.

items.title: TEM Agent connects natural-language microscope control with computing and data tools
items.what_changed: Newly discovered October report describes tested natural-language microscope control through constrained MCP actions, tomography and ptychography workflows, and links to NERSC and Crucible. It reports processing in seconds instead of hours and documents an initial sample-tilt error requiring human correction.
items.significance: Could make sophisticated microscopy workflows more accessible and reduce analysis bottlenecks; this is supervised research capability, not evidence of error-free autonomy.
items.affiliation_evidence: Official article credits DOE Office of Science support without Genesis attribution. Peter Ercius participates in Ceder's Genesis autonomous-lab team (registry project A-WILD), but shared personnel do not establish that TEM Agent belongs to that award. No project-specific linkage verified.
items.deduplication_note: Absent from archive and review candidates. Foundry republication is treated as the same article; separate from SYNAPS-I X-ray imaging articles.
